Priya Singh: Hi all, day 2 here. Following the K8s onboarding doc but I think my kubeconfig got merged weirdly. When I `kubectl get pods -n sandbox` I get "Error from server (NotFound): namespaces \"sandbox\" not found" even though the README says it should exist. I also see two contexts and one user that looks like someone else. Can someone help me sort the kubeconfig merge + get sandbox access?

Luis Gomez: welcome Priya! :wave: quick checklist: 1) `echo $KUBECONFIG` (on mac/linux) or check `%KUBECONFIG%` on Windows, 2) `kubectl config get-contexts`, 3) `kubectl config view --flatten --minify`. Often kubeconfig merge order means the last file overrides.

Priya Singh: `echo $KUBECONFIG` -> `/Users/priya/.kube/config:/Users/priya/.kube/okta-config`, `kubectl config get-contexts` ->
```
CURRENT   NAME                 CLUSTER              AUTHINFO
          redwood-dev          gke-redwood-dev      admin@work
*         redwood-onboarding   gke-redwood-dev      priya@okta
```

Priya Singh: but `kubectl config view --flatten --minify` shows user `admin@work` (weird).

Luis Gomez: that explains it. When you have KUBECONFIG pointing to multiple files, `--minify` flattens the current context but the auth info can come from a different file depending on merge order. Try `KUBECONFIG=/Users/priya/.kube/okta-config kubectl config view --minify` to inspect the okta-only view.

Priya Singh: ok running that now... it shows user `priya@okta` and the context `redwood-onboarding`. Good catch. But still `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n sandbox` -> "no".

Luis Gomez: namespace access is RBAC. New hires usually get either a RoleBinding to their Okta principal in the namespace or we give a short-lived SA token for demos. @eng-infra-bot can you open an INFRA ticket for Priya sandbox access? Note preference: RoleBinding for now.

eng-infra-bot: Created INFRA-4001: "Sandbox namespace access - Priya Singh" assigned to @platform-oncall. ETA 2h.

DevEx Bot: Tip: to avoid merge confusion long-term we recommend a single merged kubeconfig under `~/.kube/config` created with `kubectl config view --flatten > ~/.kube/config` after verifying the correct order. Also you can set `KUBECONFIG` only when switching clusters.

platform-oncall: Hi Priya 44b. I can grant the RoleBinding to `priya@okta` in `sandbox` for 48h. If you prefer SA token instead (for CI/testing) say so. Applying RoleBinding now.

platform-oncall: RoleBinding applied. Command to verify:
```
kubectl auth can-i list pods -n sandbox
kubectl get pods -n sandbox
```

Priya Singh: running `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n sandbox` -> yes. `kubectl get pods -n sandbox` -> lists a few demo pods. Thanks so much! :tada:

Luis Gomez: nice. If you want to clean up your kubeconfig to be less error-prone: backup `~/.kube/config` then run `kubectl config view --flatten > ~/.kube/config` and confirm `kubectl config get-contexts` shows the right user/context.

Priya Singh: will do. One last question: are the onboarding demos allowed to create ClusterRoleBindings? I got an error earlier when running a sample that tried to create cluster-scoped resources.

platform-oncall: No, onboarding demos should be namespaced only. For cluster-scoped resources open a ticket and we can approve on a case-by-case basis. For most tutorials use namespace `sandbox` and avoid cluster roles.

Priya Singh: got it, thanks everyone! I'll update ONBOARD-118 to mark K8s access done.
